entries.title: Exact row-extension threshold (draft proof)
entries.statement: DRAFT, author proof pending independent review. Let n>=2, r>=0, D be a real (n-1)-by-n matrix, and A append X^T. If d=s_min(D)<=r, then s_min(A)<=r. If d>r, choose unit kernel v and orthonormal right singular pairs (v_i,s_i). Exactly s_min(A)<=r iff |<v,X>|^2<=r^2(1+sum_i <v_i,X>^2/(s_i^2-r^2)). This is a Schur-complement identity, not the coefficient-one conjecture.
assumptions: Use the cone formula only when d>r; deficient rank is handled separately

entries.title: Signed replacement estimate still missing
entries.statement: UNPROVED INPUT. Let D_k have k-1 iid standard Gaussian rows and n-k iid sign rows, all independent, and let Q_mu(D,r) be the exact row-extension probability. The algebraic identity p_sign(epsilon)-F_n(epsilon)=sum_k E(Q_sign(D_k,r)-Q_Gaussian(D_k,r)), r=epsilon/sqrt(n), is proved in the draft; deficient-skeleton terms cancel. The missing estimate sum_k E(Q_sign-Q_Gaussian)<=epsilon-F_n(epsilon)+q^n, uniformly for one q<1, is equivalent to the coefficient-one conjecture and is not proved.
assumptions: Mutually independent mixed rows; F_n is the finite-n real Gaussian CDF

entries.title: Flat Hadamard obstruction (draft proof)
entries.statement: DRAFT COUNTEREXAMPLE, review pending. For n=2^m>=2 delete the all-ones row of a Sylvester Hadamard matrix to get D. All chosen singular directions are flat. At r=1/[8(n+1)], an independent sign row has conditional small-singular probability binomial(n,n/2)/2^n>=1/(n+1), while a Gaussian row has probability <=2r. Their difference is >=3/[4(n+1)]. Flatness alone does not imply pointwise Gaussian domination. This does not refute an average over iid random skeletons or estimates imposing large arithmetic LCD.
assumptions: Independent product sign or standard Gaussian last row

entries.title: Refuted shortcut: flatness gives domination
entries.statement: REFUTED ROUTE. The proposed statement that every rectangular sign skeleton with flat kernel and flat orthonormal singular directions obeys Q_sign(D,r)<=Q_Gaussian(D,r)+exp(-cn) uniformly for some c>0 is false. The Hadamard family gives a positive threshold with excess >=3/[4(n+1)]. Orthogonal sign projections are not generally independent, because their squared norms sum to the deterministic value n.
assumptions: This is a failed proof route, not an accepted theorem
No arithmetic or typical-spectrum hypotheses are imposed in the refuted route

entries.title: Gaussian finite-n scope correction (draft)
entries.statement: DRAFT SCOPE CORRECTION, review pending. For an iid standard real Gaussian n-by-n G_n and each fixed t>=0, P(sqrt(n) s_min(G_n)<=t) converges as n->infinity to 1-exp(-t-t^2/2). The limiting expression is not the finite-n CDF: for n=1 the CDF is erf(t/sqrt(2)), with derivative sqrt(2/pi) at zero. The finite-n bound P(sqrt(n) s_min(G_n)<=t)<=t is separate. The old C0029-A001 attempt incorrectly used equality for finite n. Supporting primary source: Rudelson-Vershynin ICM 2010, Theorem 3.1 and equation (3.2).
assumptions: The asymptotic statement fixes t before letting n tend to infinity

relations.rationale: The exact replacement identity uses the exact row-extension event: schur states “Exactly s_min(A)<=r iff ...”; replacement states “sum_k E(Q_sign-Q_Gaussian)”. Neither asserts the missing inequality.
obstruction gives excess “>=3/[4(n+1)]” on flat Hadamard skeletons; shortcut proposes excess “<=exp(-cn)” uniformly. Polynomial excess eventually exceeds any such exponential.
